proposals.hypothesis: Li2O is a wide-gap, Li-rich, insulating oxide with no polyanion. Its only anion is O2-, which is a weak reductant, so it may avoid the P-S, B-S and S-Cl exchange seen with the polyanionic oxides and the halides. At the Li6PS5Cl contact it could form Li2S and phosphate or chloride products with a smaller reaction energy than the chloride coatings. This tests a simple binary oxide family that has not been evaluated yet.
proposals.motivation: The chloride Li2MgCl4 and Li2ZnCl4 gave the lowest penalties so far (0.189, bin 9), but both still formed PCl5/SCl4 at the sulfide contact and missed the 0.05 eV/atom threshold. Oxides with P/B/Zr polyanions and LiF all produced worse or similar exchange products. Li2O is a different, polyanion-free chemistry that could reduce the sulfide-side exchange.

proposal.motivation: The halide family gave the best penalties so far (Li2MgCl4 and Li2ZnCl4 at 0.189, bin 9; LiF at 0.310, bin 15). Chlorides are no longer available, so a multication fluoride is the nearest untested halide.
